text:
alex: Heads up — hit a weird race during a state move/import. Tried to consolidate tfstate blobs for eu-west, the import timed out on our proxy and CI retried, ended up provisioning the same GPU nodepool twice. Attaching snippets.

priya: @alex can you paste the first error and the CI run id? :eyes:

alex: sure — CI id repo/infra#452. Initial error was a 504 from the corporate proxy during `terraform import` followed by a second apply that didn't see the lock.
```
Error: failed to import resource
caused by: Post "https://storage.azure.com/...": net/http: request canceled (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)
```

infra-bot: tf-locker: lock acquired on dynamodb tfstate-locks key="workspace/eu-west/gpu" owner=ci-run-452 ttl=30s

sam: this looks like our lock TTL is too short for blob/az requests when the proxy spikes. If TTL expires the apply path rechecks and then proceeds. Azure blob lease timeouts can also hide the object from the backend.

becka: GitOps reconciler saw the partial import (no resources in git state) and immediately triggered an apply to reconcile desired state -> triggered the duplicate provisioning. We need a pause between manual imports and auto-reconciles.

mike: Recovery plan I suggest: 1) cordon/drain duplicate nodes and scale down duplicate nodepool, 2) identify which tfstate contains the orphaned resources, 3) remove orphan resources from the wrong workspace with `terraform state rm`, or import them correctly, 4) if lock item is stuck, delete in Dynamo.

alex: tried `terraform state rm` but backend responded "no such object" because the blob index got compacted after partial write. Ended up using `az storage blob lease` to temporarily lock the blob and download the raw state. Command we used: 
```
az storage blob lease acquire --blob-name tfstate-eu-west.tfstate --container-name tfstate --account-name infra-state --lease-duration 60
az storage blob download --container-name tfstate --name tfstate-eu-west.tfstate --file /tmp/state.json
```

priya: For short-term mitigations: increase dynamo/lock TTL to 120s, add an explicit `pause-on-manual-state-mod` label to the GitOps pipeline, and add retries with exponential backoff + jitter on the proxy path.

sam: pushing a small gate script that checks `dynamodb:GetItem` for an active lock before any import/apply and sleeps + retry if found. PR: https://git.internal/r/infra/lock-gate/pull/6

becka: I rolled back the GitOps reconcile for 45m, scaled the mistaken nodepool down, and marked the workspace read-only in the console while Alex did the blob recovery.

mike: post-cleanup checklist: run `terraform plan -target=module.gpu_pool` in the main workspace, ensure no duplicate resources show up in Azure portal, and then re-enable reconciler with a 5m cooldown.

alex: status update: orphaned pool deprovisioned, main workspace state restored from the leased blob, dynamo lock TTL increased. We still need a short postmortem and an ops doc for manual imports + gitops coexistence.

infra-bot: incident created INC-210854 — labels: tfstate, import-race, gpu-provisioning

becka: assigning follow-ups: @sam will land the lock-gate PR, @mike will write the canary plan, @alex will draft the postmortem.

alex: thanks all — will follow up with a concise postmortem later today. :thumbsup:
